bug_info.bug_desc: The signal instr_executing is asserted for single-cycle instructions when the IF stage stalls (instr_new_i remains high), because it depends on instr_new_i OR ~instr_multicycle_done_q. Since instr_multicycle_done_q is never set for single-cycle instructions, instr_executing stays high during IF stalls, which keeps data_req_id, mult_en_id, and div_en_id asserted. This prevents the register file write enable (regfile_we) from deasserting, causing continuous writes to the register file with stale ALU results.
bug_info.fix_hint: Modify the instr_executing logic to only evaluate instr_multicycle_done_q for multi-cycle instructions (load/store, multiply/divide, branches, jumps). For single-cycle instructions, instr_executing should deassert once the instruction has been accepted and executed, regardless of IF stalls. This can be achieved by gating the ~instr_multicycle_done_q term with a condition that indicates a multi-cycle instruction is currently in the ID stage.
